paper.title_en: Probing fundamental cosmology with the dark ages 21-cm signal
paper.abstract_en: The cosmic dark ages offer a pristine, astrophysically unadulterated window into fundamental cosmology. Unlike the two-dimensional snapshot provided by the cosmic microwave background (CMB), the redshifted 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen enables a three-dimensional tomographic view of cosmic evolution, observable through both the sky-averaged (global) signal and through analyzing spatial fluctuations across scales (power spectrum). In this work, we present comparative observational forecasts for three representative non-standard scenarios: Excess Radio Background (ERB) model (A_{r} = 0.001), co-SIMP dark matter model (C_{\mathrm{int}} = 1.5) and the Starobinsky (ST) model of inflation featuring a localized primordial power suppression at k_{\text{dip}} \approx 7.5\text{ Mpc}^{-1}. Assuming a single-antenna spectrometer on the lunar far side integrating for 1000 hours, we find that the standard \Lambda CDM global signal can be detected relative to null at 4.12\sigma . The co-SIMP global signal is detectable relative to null at 4.67\sigma and can be distinguished from standard \Lambda CDM at 2.76\sigma significance, whereas the ERB model is detectable relative to null at 3.86\sigma but can only be distinguished from standard cosmology at 0.29\sigma . For spatial power spectrum observations over 10,000 hours using a compact 25\text{ km}^{2} lunar far-side interferometer array, we forecast detection significances relative to null of 1.97\sigma (\Lambda CDM), 2.26\sigma (ERB), 4.50\sigma (co-SIMP), and 1.61\sigma (ST). The spatial power spectrum enables model-discrimination significances relative to standard cosmology of 3.32\sigma for the co-SIMP model, 0.29\sigma for the ERB model, and 0.13\sigma for the ST model.
